summary: Southeast Asia's main startup and VC hub, home to most regional fund HQs and many unicorns (Grab, Sea, Carousell, Ninja Van). Strong government co-investment via Startup SG, EDB, SEEDS Capital and SGInnovate, plus deep-tech spinouts from NUS, NTU and A*STAR.
startup_visa: EntrePass (Ministry of Manpower) for venture-backed or innovative founders, https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/entrepass ; ONE Pass for top talent
company_setup: Private limited (Pte Ltd) registered online with ACRA via BizFile+ in about a day, roughly S$315 in fees; foreigners need a locally resident director, usually via a corporate secretary or nominee service, so remote incorporation is possible.

grants.name: Startup SG Founder
grants.amount: up to S$50,000 startup capital grant plus mentorship via Accredited Mentor Partners
grants.eligibility: First-time founders, Singaporean/PR majority, company under 6 months old at application

grants.name: Startup SG Tech
grants.amount: Proof-of-Concept and Proof-of-Value grants (caps per current guidelines, roughly S$250k to S$500k+)
grants.eligibility: Singapore-registered tech startups with 30%+ local shareholding developing proprietary tech

grants.name: Startup SG Equity
grants.amount: government co-investment alongside qualified third-party investors
grants.eligibility: Innovative Singapore-based tech startups raising from approved investors

grants.name: Startup SG Loan
grants.amount: government risk-shared loans for working capital and equipment
grants.eligibility: Startups and young SMEs with 30% local shareholding

grants.name: Startup SG Talent
grants.amount: talent and internship support schemes for startups

grants.name: Enterprise Development Grant (EDG)
grants.amount: up to 50% of qualifying project costs
grants.eligibility: Singapore-registered companies with 30% local shareholding, financially viable

grants.name: SEEDS Capital co-investment
grants.amount: co-investment in deep-tech startups alongside co-investment partners
grants.eligibility: Singapore-based deep-tech startups (agrifood, advanced manufacturing, health, sustainability)

grants.name: SGInnovate deep-tech investment
grants.amount: pre-seed to Series A equity

summary: Kuala Lumpur and Penang host a growing ecosystem led by MDEC, Cradle and MRANTI, with notable companies such as Grab (founded in Malaysia), Carsome, Aerodyne and Funding Societies Malaysia. Strong government grant and fund-of-funds support, with equity crowdfunding regulated by the Securities Commission.
startup_visa: Malaysia Tech Entrepreneur Programme (MTEP, MDEC): 1-year pass for new founders, 5-year for established entrepreneurs/investors, https://www.mdec.my/programmes/mtep
company_setup: Sdn Bhd registered with SSM online (MyCoID), around RM1,000 in fees and a few days; at least one resident director is required, and foreign-owned firms face higher paid-up capital rules for some licences.

grants.name: Cradle Investment Programme (CIP) Spark
grants.amount: up to RM150,000 conditional grant over 18 months
grants.eligibility: Teams with a Malaysian member, or companies under 5 years with revenue below RM3M, owning IP

grants.name: Cradle Investment Programme (CIP) Sprint
grants.amount: up to RM600,000 conditional grant over 18 months
grants.eligibility: Sdn Bhd companies with a commercialisable product, revenue caps apply

grants.name: MRANTI Dana Pengkomersialan
grants.amount: commercialisation funding (amounts per call)

grants.name: MTDC technology funds
grants.amount: commercialisation and technology acquisition grants

grants.amount: government-backed tech financing (soft loans)

grants.amount: grants, Malaysia Digital status incentives and market access
grants.eligibility: Digital tech companies with Malaysia Digital status

accelerators.name: Google for Startups Accelerator: Southeast Asia
accelerators.investment: no equity; cloud credits and mentoring

summary: Largest startup market in Southeast Asia, centred on Jakarta, with unicorns such as GoTo, Traveloka, Bukalapak and Xendit. Active local VCs and corporate VCs from state banks and telcos; funding cooled after 2022 but early-stage activity continues.
startup_visa: none (no dedicated startup visa; investor KITAS and Golden Visa via Immigration), https://evisa.imigrasi.go.id/
company_setup: Foreign-owned companies must be a PT PMA, with an investment plan over IDR 10bn per business line; the minimum paid-up capital was cut to IDR 2.5bn in 2025. Licensing is done online through OSS. A local PT is cheaper but needs Indonesian shareholders, so many founders use a Singapore holding company.

grants.amount: research and startup-innovation funding calls

grants.amount: incubation and acceleration support, no equity

grants.name: Ekraf creative economy support

accelerators.name: Google for Startups Accelerator: Southeast Asia
accelerators.investment: no equity; cloud credits and mentoring

notes: Komdigi replaced Kominfo in late 2024. 1000 Startup Digital and the ANGIN site could not be confirmed online in Oct 2026 and are omitted. Few published accelerator deadlines found.

summary: Bangkok-centred ecosystem with strong corporate venture activity from banks and conglomerates (SCB, Kasikorn, Krungsri, PTT) and agencies NIA and depa. Notable companies include Flash Express, Ascend Money and LINE MAN Wongnai.
startup_visa: SMART Visa (S category for startup founders, endorsed by NIA/depa/other agencies), https://smart-visa.boi.go.th/ ; Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa also available
company_setup: Private limited company registered with DBD; foreign majority ownership is limited by the Foreign Business Act unless BOI promotion or a Foreign Business Licence is obtained. Takes about 1–3 weeks; a local lawyer is usually needed.

grants.name: NIA innovation funding (incl. Market Expansion)
grants.amount: up to THB 2M per project for Market Expansion; other open-innovation grants

grants.eligibility: Thai digital startups registered 3 years or less

summary: Fast-growing ecosystem in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi with strong engineering talent; notable companies include VNG, MoMo, Sky Mavis and VNLife. Government backing via the National Innovation Center (NIC) and the National Technology Innovation Fund.
company_setup: Foreign founders typically set up a single-member LLC with an Investment Registration Certificate then Enterprise Registration Certificate; takes about 1–2 months. Many startups use a Singapore holding company for fundraising.

grants.name: National Technology Innovation Fund (NATIF)
grants.amount: grants, soft loans and loan guarantees for tech innovation
grants.eligibility: Vietnamese enterprises with tech innovation projects

summary: Manila-centred ecosystem with fintech leaders (GCash/Mynt, Maya, PayMongo) and a legal framework under the Innovative Startup Act (RA 11337). Government grants via DOST, DTI and DICT; corporate VCs from Globe, Ayala, JG Summit and UnionBank.
startup_visa: none confirmed (Innovative Startup Act provides for a startup visa, but no dedicated programme page verified)
company_setup: Domestic or foreign stock corporation registered with the SEC (eSPARC online), plus BIR and LGU permits; foreign ownership limits apply in some sectors. Takes about 2–4 weeks.

summary: Small but growing ecosystem in Phnom Penh, with 235 startups recorded in 2025 and a National Strategy on Startup Development 2026–2030. Government support via Khmer Enterprise (MEF) and Techo Startup Center; corporate VC from Smart Axiata and Canadia.
company_setup: Private limited company registered online with the Ministry of Commerce (100% foreign ownership allowed in most sectors); takes about 1–3 weeks. Many founders use a Singapore holding company.

summary: Very early-stage ecosystem in Vientiane, supported by donors (KOICA, World Bank, DFAT) and the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, which hosted the first National Startup Fest in April 2026. The MSME and Startup Innovation Center (MSIC) is being developed with KOICA.
company_setup: Enterprise registration with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, with foreign investment approvals via the Investment Promotion Department; usually takes several weeks. Many founders use a Thai or Singapore entity for fundraising.

grants.name: National Startup Fest and MSIC incubation
grants.agency: Ministry of Industry and Commerce with KOICA and Kookmin University
grants.amount: six-month incubation for winning teams

summary: Ecosystem contracted sharply after the February 2021 military coup; many investors and accelerators stopped work. Some social-enterprise support continues in Yangon, but most international capital is unavailable.
company_setup: Private company registered online via MyCO (DICA), which is technically quick, but banking, sanctions and conflict risks make it impractical for most founders. Diaspora founders usually incorporate in Singapore or Thailand.

resources.name: DICA
resources.note: Directorate of Investment and Company Administration

notes: Post-coup conflict and sanctions since 2021: international VC is effectively unavailable. Phandeeyar's site could not be resolved in Oct 2026, so it is omitted.

summary: Small ecosystem focused on diversifying from oil and gas, led by the Brunei Economic Development Board (BEDB), which now runs DARe-era bootcamps, the iCentre incubator and Kontena Park.
company_setup: Private company limited by shares registered via the Registry of Companies (ROCBN, under the Ministry of Finance and Economy); foreign ownership allowed in many sectors, with a resident director required.

grants.name: BEDB financing and co-matching grants
grants.agency: Brunei Economic Development Board (incl. former DARe)
grants.amount: co-matching grants reported up to BND 20,000
grants.eligibility: Businesses 100% owned by Brunei citizens or PRs

resources.name: BIBD
resources.note: Bank with SME and startup financing

notes: DARe programmes now appear under BEDB; dare.gov.bn returns 404. Grant amount comes from secondary reports.

summary: Very small ecosystem in Dili supported mainly by government agencies and donors (UNDP, KOICA, ADB, World Bank). Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025, and a government business incubation centre in Dili broke ground in January 2026.
company_setup: Company registration through SERVE (one-stop shop), usually within days; foreign investment guided by TradeInvest Timor-Leste. The economy uses the US dollar.

grants.name: Business Innovation Challenge (Path to Business)
grants.agency: Ministry of Commerce and Industry with UNDP
grants.amount: equipment and materials grants

grants.name: Seed Funding Incubation (SFI)
grants.agency: UNDP Timor-Leste with IADE and KOICA
grants.amount: seed funding, training and mentoring

notes: No local VC found. Diaspora founders often use Australian or Singapore entities.
